run.procedureSummary: 1. Charge: add each crucible's cycle charge to its contents. It may sit above capacity for now. 2. Overflow: walk positions 1 to 6. Any excess over capacity leaves the crucible, which is set to exactly its capacity, and goes into the next crucible before that one is checked, so it can carry down the line. Excess from crucible 6 goes to slag and is added to the loss tally. 3. State check, on the contents after overflow: a BASE crucible with melt at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED; a SUPERHEATED crucible at or below its lower mark becomes BASE; otherwise the state stays as it is. Each crucible is checked once per cycle. 4. Draw-off: using the contents after step 3, work out all six amounts first, rounding down. BASE: floor(q/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED: floor(q/2) back to the previous crucible (position i-1); for crucible 1 that half goes to slag. Then all moves are applied at once. Returned melt can leave a crucible above capacity, and it is not corrected until the next cycle's overflow. 5. Global reset: add up all six. Only if the total is strictly above 38, set every crucible to floor(q/2), add the removed amount (q - floor(q/2)) to slag and note the cycle. At 38 or below, nothing happens.

openPoints.point: How 'halve every crucible, rounding down' applies in the global reset when a quantity is odd
openPoints.assumption: The rounding applies to what stays: the new quantity is floor(q/2) and the removed amount, q - floor(q/2), goes to slag. So for odd quantities the larger half goes to slag. This matters in cycles 1 and 4.

openPoints.point: The global reset boundary at exactly 38
openPoints.assumption: 'Strictly above 38' is read literally. The cycle 5 total is exactly 38, so no reset fires in cycle 5.
It goes to the slag pit and is added to the loss tally, as the write-up says ('not a ladle').

openPoints.point: Crucibles above capacity at the end of cycle 5 because of returned melt
openPoints.assumption: Left as they are, per the write-up ('or for good after cycle 5'). End quantities: crucible 2 holds 10 against a capacity of 8, and crucible 4 holds 7 against a capacity of 6.
The contents after step 3 (after overflow). All six amounts are worked out before anything moves, so melt returned in a cycle is not drawn again in that same cycle.
